name: Timurid Empire

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 5.5 million km2 for 1400 (high); Turchin, Adams and Hall give 4.4 million km2 for 1405 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timurid_Empire, low); the world_1400 polygon measures 5.10 million km2 (mid).

population.note: Sum of HYDE/Gapminder 1400 country series (OWID): Iran 3.75M, Iraq 1.0M, Afghanistan 1.9M, Uzbekistan 1.2M, Turkmenistan 0.2M, Tajikistan 0.3M, Azerbaijan, Armenia and eastern Anatolia ~1.0M, parts of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan ~1M = ~10-11M (low). Mid allows for HYDE undercounting Iran and Transoxiana. Seshat codes 49 million (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/370, high), which this researcher considers implausible for these lands.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Samarkand ~150,000 (Seshat), Herat, Tabriz, Isfahan, Shiraz, Bukhara.

activePersonnel.note: Timur's field army at Ankara (1402) is "reliably estimated" at 140,000, mostly cavalry (Nicolle 1983 p. 29, via the article); he led over 100,000 against Tokhtamysh in 1391 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timur). Adds garrisons and the princes' armies in Khurasan and Fars. Ibn Arabshah's 800,000 rejected. Tribal tumens were permanently embodied under Timur, so they count as active, as in mongol-empire-1241.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Further tribal contingents and sedentary (Tajik) levies (hashar) called for specific campaigns.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Siege engineers, naphtha throwers, artisans and Indian mahouts with the army.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Nomadic Turco-Mongol tribes mobilised most adult males; sedentary subjects supplied far fewer.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Horse archers, the majority of the tumens (Manz, Rise and Rule of Tamerlane, describes the army as tribal cavalry).

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: lifelong riders, continuous campaigning since 1370.

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured lancers and the guard (kheshig-type) regiments.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: lamellar and mail, horse armour for the guard.

count.note: Educated guess. Tajik and Persian foot, sappers, garrison troops.
Educated guess. Foot archers and dismounted horse archers in sieges.
32 war elephants at Ankara (Nicolle 1983, via the article), brought from the 1398 Delhi campaign; more were used as labour at Samarkand (high).
Educated guess. Trebuchets, mangonels and naphtha engines built on campaign (sieges of Aleppo and Damascus 1400-01, Baghdad 1401).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Persian and Chinese-derived siege technology.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 1.0: Timur never lost a major battle (Kondurcha 1391, Terek 1395, Delhi 1398, Ankara 1402); best-in-era.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: loyalty to Timur personally; tribal amirs reorganised under his household (Manz), fragile without him.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: thirty years of victories and plunder.

weapons.note: Anchor 4 plus: composite bow, counterweight trebuchet, naphtha; little gunpowder artillery.

ships.note: Anchor 1-2: river craft only; no navy.

fortification.note: Anchor 4 minus: walled Samarkand and Herat citadels, little new building.

logistics.note: Anchor 4 plus: herds and remounts gave strategic reach from Delhi to Ankara.

isr.note: Anchor 4 plus: merchants and spies ahead of every campaign.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) Iraq 1150 = 1,084, Iran 1 CE = 1,116, Turkey 1348 = 743 (2011 int$). Plunder from Delhi, Persia and Syria flowed to Samarkand.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A state organised around permanent campaigning.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Deported artisans in Samarkand, textiles, metalwork.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Oasis irrigation and pastoralism; Iran's agriculture damaged by the conquests.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Caravan routes of the Silk Road; few engineered roads.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Persian Gulf ports via vassal Hormuz; Caspian landings.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. No merchant marine of its own.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Herds and remounts let armies range far beyond bases where pasture existed; Timur campaigned 2,000+ km from Samarkand. Comparable to mongol-empire-1241.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (several remounts per rider), camels and oxen.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: steppe and desert depth and a harsh continental climate around Transoxiana; conquered Iran gives less.

notes: Snapshot = 1400, Timur's invasion of Syria (Aleppo, Damascus) between Delhi (1398) and Ankara (1402). Army size anchored on Nicolle's 140,000 at Ankara (an Osprey-level source, so grade C); Manz (The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane, 1989) describes the army's tribal structure but no total was found to quote. Chronicle figures (Ibn Arabshah 800,000; a German witness 1.6 million) rejected (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Ankara). Population convention: directly ruled Transoxiana, Khwarazm, Khurasan, Iran, Iraq and the southern Caucasus; vassal Georgia, Delhi and the Golden Horde excluded. Population is the weakest number: HYDE (~11M) and Seshat (49M) disagree by a factor of four.
